challenge.name: self-XSS notes app with an offline report bot (noted)

all_of: a bot renders attacker-influenced pages while holding the secret
the stored XSS is confined to the attacker's own account
the bot has no route to the public internet
any_of: the login route has no CSRF protection so the session can be swapped mid-visit
the application accepts a non-HTTP scheme for the reported URL
the app itself offers a write the attacker can read back

chain.action: establish what the bot IS before designing anything: which account it holds and where the secret lives
chain.why: the bot registers its own account and stores the flag there, so the payload must reach the bot's own rendering, not yours

chain.action: resolve every URL in the payload to the application's INTERNAL address
chain.why: an offline bot cannot resolve the public hostname, and the failure is completely silent

chain.action: load the victim's secret page into a NAMED window by top-level navigation
chain.why: a top-level navigation sends a SameSite=Lax cookie where an iframe does not

chain.action: swap the session with a form POST to the unprotected login route so the attacker's stored XSS renders
chain.why: the XSS then runs on the application origin and is same-origin with the already-rendered secret window

chain.action: write the secret back through the application's own API instead of out to the network
chain.why: no egress exists; a note in the attacker's account is readable afterwards

first_confirming_probe.request: report a page whose only job is to post a fixed marker back through the application's own write API using the internal address
first_confirming_probe.expected: the marker appears in your own account, proving the reported page executed and the internal address is correct
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: no marker appears, meaning the scheme is not executed by the bot or the address is unreachable

blast_radius: each report spawns a browser and a fresh account server-side; keep reports serial. The stored payload runs in your own account only.

verification.evidence: the flag arrived as the content of a note in our own account and was read from the live GET /notes response

reuse_when: a headless bot has no internet and the exfiltration channel must be the application itself
a challenge hinges on which cookie a navigation carries
a payload must run on the target origin but the only injection is self-XSS
known_traps: target=_blank carries implicit noopener, which puts the new window in a SEPARATE browsing-context group so window.open('',name) cannot resolve the name and silently returns a blank window; the symptom is indistinguishable from popup blocking -- use a NAMED target
a top-level data: URL does not execute when Chrome is given it as a command-line argument but does under the bot's CDP-driven navigation; test the path the bot actually uses
with no egress, make the payload post its own step-by-step diagnostics back through the app; that converts a silent black box into a debugger
